stemMd: Which structure prevents food from normally entering the lower respiratory tract during swallowing?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The epiglottis contributes to closure of the laryngeal entrance.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The pancreas folds over the larynx.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The diaphragm becomes a plug inside the pharynx.

explanationMd: Swallowing coordinates movement of the larynx and closure of the airway, with the epiglottis helping shield the laryngeal entrance. This directs the food bolus toward the oesophagus. The structure belongs to the upper airway, not the abdomen or urinary system.

distractorRationale.c: The iris is part of the eye.
distractorRationale.d: The ureter carries urine from kidney to bladder.
distractorRationale.b: The pancreas is an abdominal organ.
distractorRationale.e: The diaphragm is the main respiratory muscle, not a pharyngeal plug.
